text:
Alex M: incident-bot just paged for REDWOOD-INCIDENT-459: embed-generation latency p95 > 500ms in us-west-2 for model redwood-v1. Not seeing error spikes but throughput steady. Primary oncall?

oncall-bot: Paging @Mira S, @Sam R (rotational) — alert: `embed_latency_p95_us_west` threshold breached at 2025-03-20T18:11:40Z

Mira S: I'm primary until 18:00 PT. I can take initial triage. I'll check the autoscaler and runtime metrics.

Sam R: I'm secondary until 19:00 PT. There's a scheduled handoff at 18:30 — we have a 30m single-coverage gap 18:00-18:30 unless someone covers.

Jordan P: I can cover 18:00-18:30 if needed. Ping me when you want me to jump in.

Mira S: Runbook steps I'm following: 1) check autoscaler events in Console (/runbooks/latency-warnings) 2) tail runtime logs: `kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=inference --since=15m` 3) check KV cache hit rate & prefix churn on the infra dashboard.

Alex M: quick note — CS reports customer "Acme Analytics" sees timeouts for batch embedding jobs. Potential SLA impact for Dedicated customers.

Nina (CS): Acme confirms timeouts on >=5% of jobs in last 10m. They're on Dedicated plan, SLA 99.9% for throughput >=100 qps. They're flagged as high-priority.

Mira S: initial mitigation: scale the GPU pool for us-west-2. Planning to run: 
```
infractl scale pool us-west-2-gpu-pool --add 2
```
Executing now.

oncall-bot: Scale job accepted. Expected worker registration ~2m.

Sam R: while we scale, we should consider temporarily tuning alerts to avoid paging on transient spikes. Proposal: bump critical p95 from 500ms -> 700ms for 15m, with an audit entry and explicit rollback. This is a mitigation to prevent alert storms while we stabilize.

Alex M: caution — changing threshold affects SLO/SLA breach detection. We must record the change in this thread and in the incident timeline. Also notify support so CS can adjust comms.

Mira S: agreed. I'll do the temporary change with an audit note: 
```
alertctl update embed_latency_p95_us_west --critical 700ms --note "temp during scaling 1748509200"
```
Applying now.

support-bot: Audit log created: alert `embed_latency_p95_us_west` critical changed 500ms -> 700ms by Mira S at 2025-03-20T18:12:30Z (temporary 15m).

Jordan P: scaling finished — +2 GPUs are online and registered to pool. Seeing pod counts increase.

Mira S: metrics: p95 dropped from ~820ms -> ~430ms over the last 10m. Looks stable. Rolling alert threshold back to 500ms now.

support-bot: Audit log: alert `embed_latency_p95_us_west` restored 700ms -> 500ms by Mira S at 2025-03-20T18:28:10Z.

Alex M: CS notified Acme with mitigation update and validation steps. They will run a few representative jobs and confirm.

Nina (CS): Acme confirms retries succeeded and no further timeouts after scale. They requested an RCA and whether this affected SLA reporting.

Mira S: quick RCA notes: root cause appears to be a recent config change to prefix cache TTL that increased cache miss storms under certain traffic patterns, causing KV backend pressure and tail latency. Mitigation: revert TTL change in next patch and add a canary monitor for prefix churn. Filing issue infra#2345.

Sam R: action item on rotations: we had a 30m single-coverage window because the scheduled handoff didn't align with the escalation window. I'll propose an overflow pager or shift adjustment so 18:00-19:00 always has primary+secondary overlap.

Alex M: good call. Also: include the alert threshold change step and audit entries in the postmortem timeline. We should document the temporary threshold policy for future on-call guidance.

Mira S: marking incident mitigated. I'll create the postmortem draft and link infra#2345 + the audit logs.

oncall-bot: Incident REDWOOD-INCIDENT-459 marked mitigated by Mira S. :white_check_mark:

Alex M: thanks everyone — great coordination. If anyone has follow-ups, add them to the postmortem thread.
